text:
**Short answer:** A pellet smoker barely draws power once it's running, so a power station of about 1 kWh handles an overnight cook. Get one with a decent surge rating for the igniter.

**Why this works**
- Pellet grills have a short igniter burst, then a small steady draw. One test of a Z Grills on a Jackery Explorer 1000 measured about 194 W at start-up, 35 W while cooking, and 210 Wh over 6 hours. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight) estimates a 12-hour overnight cook at roughly 450–750 Wh.
- [Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill) says a 1,024 Wh unit covers a full overnight cook and a 288 Wh unit covers about five hours. It warns that a 300 W inverter with a 600 W surge is marginal, because the igniter can pull 350–500 W for several minutes. So pick a unit with at least a 600 W continuous rating.
- Don't use electric-smoker figures. [Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-smoker/) assumes about 1,000 W, which is a different appliance and far more power-hungry than a pellet grill.

**What I'd buy**
1. **BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, $449):** This is the best fit for one overnight cook. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight) says it covers one night but is "back late November", so it may not be in stock yet. [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180).
2. **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W inverter, $899):** This suits a multi-night campsite trip, since it covers two or three cooks. It's in stock now, and Dealectric lists a code that takes $44.95 off. [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).

Dealectric is the seller of both, so check the price elsewhere too.

**Budget or small-grill option:** The [Grilla Power Station](https://www.grillagrills.com/product/1197809) ($359.99) is sold for pellet grills. It's rated for a 10-hour run time and 300 W output. That 300 W output is the marginal class Volt & Valley warns about, so check your grill's igniter draw first.

**Caveats**
- Check the data plate on your grill. Igniter draw varies by model.
- Cold or windy nights push the fan and auger toward the top of the 450–750 Wh range.
- Phones and lights on the same battery cut your runtime.
- [GearBrain's video summary](https://open.video/%40gearbrain/v/can-a-portable-power-station-run-a-pellet-grill) suggests testing a full startup-to-shutdown cycle with a watt meter before you rely on it.
- BLUETTI's own [guide](https://www.bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/how-long-can-bluetti-power-pellet-grill-smoker) assumes a higher 150–250 W average draw. If your grill is closer to that, size up.
